To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the LPC, a widely studied electrophysiological correlate of recognition, reflects mnemonic strength, and not recollection versus familiarity; (b) the LPC dissociation is not specific for the RK procedure; and (c) the LPC dissociates between R and K experience, even in the absence of a mnemonic difference between these responses.
the electrophysiology of the remember–know procedure is confounded with strength, and cannot be interpreted as evidence for dual-process theory of recognition.

the electrophysiology of recognition memory is confounded by mnemonic strength.
